stories.headline: Ukraine targets Moscow with massive drone strike as Russian election concludes
stories.body:
Ukraine launched a massive drone attack against targets in Russia as voting ended in Russia's parliamentary election. The vote was the first parliamentary election in Russia since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022.

The political party United Russia received nearly 58 percent of the party-list vote. That total came with about 58 percent of precincts counted across the country. Official election figures showed that total voter turnout stood at 56.66 percent when the polls closed.

Government authorities in Kyiv denounced voting in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. Kyiv called the voting illegal. Ukrainian officials urged foreign governments not to recognize the election results. Russian election chief Ella Pamfilova said cyberattacks targeted Russia's electronic voting system during the election process.

Russia's Defence Ministry reported that its forces shot down 1,110 Ukrainian drones across Russia, Crimea, and the Black Sea. Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin gave a different figure for intercepted weapons. Sobyanin said more than 1,600 drones were intercepted and shot down in total. He said 450 of those drones were aimed at Moscow.

A drone strike caused damage to a facility at the Moscow oil refinery. In the town of Sofyino, a drone struck a three-storey residential building. A 44-year-old woman was killed in Sofyino during that strike. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine used domestically produced Flamingo cruise missiles to strike targets in Moscow.

Attacks also took place inside Ukraine. Ukrainian officials said nine people were killed in Russian attacks in the Kyiv and Sumy regions on Saturday. Three children were among the dead in those attacks.

stories.headline: US warns citizens in Iran as military tensions rise and Houthis fire missile
stories.body:
The US Virtual Embassy in Iran issued a security alert for American citizens. The embassy urged Americans to leave Iran immediately. It told Americans to avoid travelling to Iran for any reason.

US President Donald Trump said he is in a deciding mode regarding potential military action, continued economic pressure, or a deal with Iran. Officials in Tehran said Iran learned the US may be planning new strikes. Tehran warned of retaliation without limitations. Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned that all US bases and interests in the region will face continuous and painful attacks if Washington resumes military action. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said its aerospace force tracked and destroyed a US military MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz.

In Saudi Arabia, coalition forces intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh. Coalition forces reported attempted attacks targeting Bish, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Saudi Arabia conducted 28 air strikes targeting the governorates of Taiz, Al-Jawf, and Marib. UK Cabinet minister Bridget Phillipson said Donald Trump's war with Iran will make the UK's upcoming budget more difficult due to oil supply disruptions and inflation.

US President Donald Trump stated he is in a 'deciding mode' regarding potential military action, continued economic pressure, or a deal with Iran.
Tehran stated it learned the US may be planning new strikes and warned of retaliation without limitations.
Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned that all US bases and interests in the region will face continuous and painful attacks if Washington resumes military action against Tehran.

stories.headline: German Chancellor Merz cancels UN trip following state election defeats
stories.body:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called his party's state election performance in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern a disaster. Merz said he would remain in office despite the result.

In Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, public broadcasters projected the far-right AfD party to win 38% of the vote. The SPD followed in second place on 35%. Merz's party, the CDU, secured 4.9 percent of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. That result marked the party's worst state election performance in that region since 1949.

In Berlin's state election, political party Die Linke led projections with nearly 26% of the vote. The CDU placed second in Berlin on 19%. After the election losses, Merz cleared his calendar. Merz skipped a planned trip to New York for the UN General Assembly.

Personal approval ratings for Merz hover just above 10 percent. Across Germany, the far-right AfD leads national opinion polls with about 30 percent support.

stories.headline: US and China discuss AI safety mechanisms before White House summit
stories.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng led talks in New York. The meeting took place at JPMorgan Chase's headquarters and lasted around eight hours.

The US proposed creating a US-China AI dialogue. This proposal includes a notification mechanism for high-level national security incidents resulting from AI. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said export controls on advanced AI chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment were not part of the mechanism.

The talks took place before a scheduled summit meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The leaders are scheduled to hold a summit meeting at the White House on Thursday. A trade truce agreed by both nations in Busan, South Korea, in October 2025 is scheduled to expire on November 10.

In related developments, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called for a worldwide pacing of frontier AI development requiring cooperation with China. China released the third iteration of its AI safety governance framework. The framework addresses risks from AI agents, cybersecurity threats from frontier models, and recursive self-improvement.

stories.headline: Delhi voter roll revision leads to widespread notices and political criticism
stories.body:
The Election Commission of India launched a voter roll review in Delhi on May 14. The Special Intensive Revision exercise has led to millions of notices sent to voters. Delhi is among 19 states and Union Territories included in the third phase of the process.

Officials issued notices to 34.5% of men on Delhi's draft electoral roll. Notices went to 33.4% of women and 50% of transgender individuals on the draft roll. In total, 59,791 notices had no reason listed against them.

Not being mapped to the previous review accounted for 42% of the notices issued. Name mismatches with the previous electoral roll accounted for 41% of notices. Parent name mismatches comprised 24% of notices, and self-name mismatches comprised 17%. Discrepancies in age differences accounted for 16% of notices.

Prominent political and official figures received notices under the process. Served individuals included LK Advani, Jagdeep Dhankhar, S Jaishankar, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, Manish Sisodia, and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta received a notice because the age difference between her and her parents appeared under 15 years. Former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B Lokur received a notice because the recorded age gap between him and his grandfather was 40 years or less.

Shyam Mukhija, aged 125 from Old Delhi's Sadar Bazar assembly constituency, was the oldest person served a notice due to a self-name mismatch. Deceased former official Bibek Debroy also received a notice because his name appeared on the flagged draft rolls. Debroy was the former chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

More than 80.62 lakh voter names were deleted from draft rolls after being marked as shifted or absent. Only 6.66 lakh Form-6 applications were submitted for inclusion. Authorities received 84,263 Form-6 applications between August 31 and September 19, after receiving 2,12,400 applications up to August 30. In Bihar, a similar review saw the total electorate decrease from 7.89 crore to about 7.42 crore. That decrease occurred even though 21.53 lakh electors were added through Form-6 applications.

Lawyer Kapil Sibal described the exercise as a special intensive deletion aimed at removing valid voters. The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office said disposal of notices will be completed by October 29, 2026. Authorities will publish the final electoral roll on November 4, 2026.

stories.headline: Crime Branch takes over probe into IIT Bombay student death after protests
stories.body:
Mumbai Police transferred an investigation into the death of an IIT Bombay student to the Crime Branch. An Assistant Commissioner of Police will lead the investigation.

Sahil Wakode, a 20-year-old second-year student of energy science and engineering, died by suicide in his hostel room. His death was the third suicide on the campus this year. An invigilating professor reported Sahil after finding him with a phone during an examination. IIT Bombay said Sahil was caught using a mobile phone to upload an exam paper onto the ChatGPT chatbot.

Sahil's father filed an FIR against Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, alleging three months of harassment. Police charged Doolla and unidentified persons with abetment to suicide and violations of the SC/ST Act. Sahil's family refused to claim his body from Rajawadi Hospital for seven hours until police assured them the case went to the Crime Branch.

The Faculty Forum of IIT Bombay defended Doolla, saying he executed approved exam procedures. IIT Bombay Director Shireesh Kedare denied caste discrimination, saying student caste information remains confidential. Kedare agreed to 18 demands from protesting students, including replacing ceiling fans with wall-mounted fans in hostels. Student demands included Doolla's suspension and an independent probe committee.

IIT Kharagpur Director sent a message reminding students that admission serves as evidence of sustained effort.
